01.reason: The Sages apportion wine to Nakdimon's daughter-in-law, she blesses them, and they withhold amen: real events, but a brief incident cited as legal evidence, mostly ruling and speech.

02.reason: Only a background statement of who was married to whom; no event is narrated within the passage.

03.reason: A habitual manner of speech by R. Abbahu; speech only, no event, no conflict.

04.reason: Rav and Rav Yehuda walking behind a woman, and their exchange about seclusion: a real setting and implied action, but mainly dialogue.

05.reason: A man snatches coins from another, throws them to a woman to betroth her, and the case comes before Rava: several narrated actions resolved by a ruling, the cow-case shape.

06.reason: A man acts improperly and Rav Kahana has him flogged: an act and a consequential response, but only alluded to in one line.

07.reason: A man comes before Rabban Gamliel with a claim and receives a parable in reply; coming before a rabbi plus speech, nothing else happens.

08.reason: One event (an ox seized) followed by a dispute before Rav Nahman and his ruling; nothing changes afterwards (Jeff 2026-10-25).

09.reason: A famine in Rav Yosef's years and the Sages' request that he pray, which he refuses; an event frame but mainly speech within the passage.

10.reason: R. Hanina's habit of sending money, then one day his wife delivers it and returns reporting what she heard: a habitual frame followed by a one-time event.

11.reason: A betrothed couple comes before Rav Yosef with claims; coming before a rabbi is the only event.

12.reason: Exegetical derivation of the dates of Moses' birth and death; a calendrical proof, not a narrated story.

13.reason: Ravina asks Rav Ashi whether he may take his orphan nephew's wine along with his own and is told to go; a question and ruling with no further narrated change.

14.reason: Ben Azzai reports finding a genealogical scroll and quotes its contents; a single act cited as evidence, leading nowhere.

15.reason: An incident named only by its ruling (Rabbi gave one-twelfth) within legal argument; a single act with no narrative.

16.reason: A document brought before R. Abbahu, who considers validating it and is corrected by R. Yirmeya; a case before a rabbi plus scholarly exchange.

17.reason: Two one-line precedents (Rav Kahana accepting a cloth, Mar bar Rav Ashi overpaying for one) cited as evidence within legal discussion; single acts leading nowhere.

18.reason: Part of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's deathbed narrative: he summons his sons, each enters, and he transmits wisdom and the office of Nasi; a sequence of events.

19.reason: A man testifies before R. Yehoshua ben Levi and the rabbi elevates the subject to Levite status: a case before a rabbi whose ruling is itself a status-changing act, borderline per the 65a line.

20.reason: The Sages ask R. Abbahu where R. Elai is and he answers in a riddle; speech only, no conflict.
